HEEWON STYLE — a KOREAN WEBTOON movie still PAINTED like a premium digital painting, the look of a dramatic manhwa cover. A 2:1 movie frame composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop (nothing important at the top or bottom edge). The shot the scene names (wide establishing, two-shot, close-up, over-the-shoulder) from a dramatic camera angle (low three-quarter, worm's-eye, high overhead or dutch), never a flat straight-on catalogue pose. Named characters' FACES are drawn exactly like the attached character sheet: the same confident ink linework drawn BOLD and THICK with real line weight — a heavy tapered black contour around the whole silhouette and the hair mass, medium lines for folds and features, fine lines only for lashes and loose strands and manhwa face design (eye shape, brows, nose, jaw, hairline and hair), recognisably those characters, in the clothes the scene gives them. KOREAN FACES on everyone in frame: living eyes with WHITE sclera, a catchlight, and BLACK ink-black iris and pupil (never brown, hazel, amber, blue, grey or green, never the whole eyeball painted solid black); a low soft Korean nasal bridge, never a high European nose. EVERYTHING ELSE IS PAINTED: visible textured brushwork — loose digital-paint strokes and dry-brush, charcoal-like hatching that follow every fold of the silk and every plate of armour, the shadows built from layered strokes, the brightest ridges laid in with single confident strokes, a faint paper-and-canvas grain; at the edges of the garments the linework breaks into loose sketchy strokes. MYTHIC PAINTED FINISH: rich saturated jewel-tone colour, never a muddy grey-brown wash; splashed sumi-ink spatter and dry-brush flying-white streaks breaking out at the frame edges; ONE bold sweeping painted ribbon of the scene's accent colour (cloth, smoke, banner, mist or light) carving across the composition like a brushstroke of legend. NOT flat cel-shading, NOT smooth airbrushed gradients, NOT a clean vector look, NOT photoreal, NOT 3D. KOREAN WEBTOON movie still, dramatic manhwa COVER, character-intro-card splash. NOT photoreal, NOT cartoon. OVER-SHOULDER from the snow rim. ONE device: the valley bowl as a vast dark cup filling two thirds of the frame. Sharp FOREGROUND: a Class 77 hwarang’s shoulder and two young disciples on their bellies, mouths open, watching. Tiny in the midground cup: Bidam a navy speck in the fog, Alchun a larger wrecking shape in the dry creek. Keep the attached valley — ridges, throat, spring, back wall. NIGHT GROUND on BLACK. Torch-ring along both crests as small bokeh. No named faces in the foreground (extras, drawn, never cloned from Bidam). No army catalog. No text. No watermark. REFERENCE SHEET. TOP ROW, left to right: LEFT face = bidam, SECOND face = alchun. Copy each face exactly; give each person the dress the scene names. SMALLER SECOND ROW, left to right: place board pl_jade_gate_valley (keep this exact architecture and ground), costume chart (cut and shape only; ignore its labels, poses and faces). KOREAN FACES on every person, named or extra: living eyes with WHITE sclera, a small catchlight, and BLACK ink-black iris and pupil (never brown, hazel, amber, honey, gold, blue, grey, green or purple). Never paint the entire eyeball solid black. A low soft Korean nasal bridge, never a high European, Roman or Persian nose. East Asian bone: single-lidded or low-creased eyes, straight or softly arched brows, broad cheekbones, flatter facial planes, warm ivory to sun-browned skin, straight coarse black hair. Never Western, Latin, or mixed-race features, never deep-set double-lidded western eyes. BIDAM — Look: Tall, handsome, clean-shaven; KIN of Kim Chunchu — same Jinji-hall bone (Bidam is Jinji's nephew, Chunchu is Jinji's grandson): the same oval Korean face, same amused half-lid, same long brow; NOT a clone, not twins. Bidam is taller, warmer. BLACK eyes (never brown, hazel, blue or grey); a small straight Korean nose with a low bridge. Short slicked-back black hair as councillor; as hwarang the hair is longer, falling past the shoulders. Dress: Councillor: his signature hybrid coat — a long white outer robe whose wide sleeves are embroidered with galloping black horses, with deep navy #141C2E bands down the lapels and a navy yoke across the shoulders, over a plum-magenta inner robe and dark sash; the bead string looped on the right wrist. Navy lives only in those lapel and shoulder bands and on the beads — never a glow. Now: Councillor: short slicked hair, NO headband, white horse-sleeve coat over plum-magenta. Colour #141C2E. ALCHUN — Look: Broader, rounder face than Bidam or Yushin; warm half-smile, a red liner wing at the outer eye; as a boy no scar and no grey. Adult: grey tied back under a dark headband, a red scar cutting the left temple, thin goatee. Unmistakably Korean: BLACK eyes (never brown, blue or grey), a low soft Korean nasal bridge. Dress: Teal-green po. Hwarang: teal po over a crimson collar and crimson sash, teal crescent-moon headband, jougwan with two tan pheasant feathers. Councillor: teal po over a rust-red inner robe, dark sash, no jougwan. High Councillor: white dragon-embroidered overcoat over magenta, teal headband. Now: Councillor (stage portrait /ch_alchun.png): grey coming, temple scar, teal over rust-red. Colour #8fb3e0. PLACE Jade Gate Valley (옥문곡 (여근곡)) — attached board /pl_jade_gate_valley.png; keep this exact architecture and ground. Jade Gate Valley (옥문곡): two long pine ridges almost meeting in a rock throat three men wide, a fog-bowl with a spring that never freezes, a steep white back wall under a hill fort, a dry creek, one great rock beside the spring. Keep this exact fold of ridges and the throat in every still. Kingdom banners: copy field colour and emblem from the attached flag_*.png ref onto period silk war-banners — tall poles behind each side, long streamers, small pennants on spear-tips and saddle-backs. Painted silk, wind-whipped, torn and smoke-stained in battle; never a flat modern flag graphic. Each side's banner colour is the clearest colour on its half of the frame, so the kingdom reads at a glance. Silla banners: blue silk with a white crescent moon. Attached flag /flag_silla.png. BACKGROUND AND LIGHT (painterly tenebrism): the background IS the place and the moment of the scene — open sky if they are in the sky, the hall if they are in a hall, the gate, the river, the snow — painted loosely in atmospheric brushwork (drifting smoke, cloud, haze, mist, falling snow, embers) in the scene's own colours, soft and out of focus, with a faint bokeh of small lights; it has colour, weather and depth — never a flat black void, never a detailed set; crowds and armies only as massed painted shapes dissolving into haze. ONE hard directional key light that belongs to the place (a brazier, a lamp, the sun through cloud, a torch, moonlight) rakes across the faces and clothes from the side or from below, modelling them in high contrast with deep painted shadows and a thin edge of the same light along the silhouette. Each character's colour lives in that light and in the atmosphere around them — never a glow aura or halo. Faces and bodies act the beat: real expressions, real weight, mid-motion. Faces from the sheet; new poses, never the sheet's stance. Each named person appears once, never cloned. Everyone wears period clothing of their own court (Korean, Tang, Yamato, Mohe furs), never European dress. No text, no speech bubbles, no panel borders, no watermark. NIGHT GROUND: the frame is built on BLACK — crushed ink-black night masses around the subject, the place pulled out of the dark only where the one key light (fire, lamp, torch, moon) falls, small warm bokeh in the black; the figure is the bright thing in a dark frame.
